events.title: Hiero II dies
events.text: Hiero II dies in his ninetieth year after more than half a century on the throne, Rome's ally since 263 BC.

events.title: Hampsicora's revolt
events.text: Titus Manlius Torquatus crushes a Sardinian revolt and the Carthaginian army sent to help it, near Carales.

events.title: Locri defects
events.text: The Greek city of Locri opens its gates to Hannibal's Carthaginians.

events.title: Petelia falls
events.text: Loyal Petelia surrenders to the Carthaginians after a long siege and famine.

events.title: Croton taken
events.text: Bruttians and Carthaginians take Croton; its people withdraw to Locri.

events.title: Envoys of Philip V
events.text: Macedonian envoys carrying Philip V's treaty with Hannibal are captured by the Roman fleet off Calabria.

events.title: Hieronymus turns
events.text: Fifteen-year-old King Hieronymus, advised by Hannibal's envoys Hippocrates and Epicydes, allies Syracuse with Carthage.

events.title: A king murdered
events.text: Conspirators stab Hieronymus in a narrow street of Leontini after about thirteen months on the throne.

events.title: Royal family killed
events.text: Syracuse proclaims a republic and kills Hiero's daughters and granddaughters.

events.title: Beneventum
events.text: Gracchus' army of volunteer slaves defeats Hanno; the survivors are rewarded with freedom.

events.title: Leontini stormed
events.text: Marcellus storms Leontini and beheads two thousand deserters; rumours of a massacre turn Syracuse against Rome.

events.title: Syracuse joins Carthage
events.text: Hippocrates and Epicydes seize Syracuse and kill the pro-Roman leaders.

events.title: Philip at Apollonia
events.text: Philip V attacks Apollonia; a Roman fleet from Brundisium surprises him and he burns his own ships.

events.title: Assault by sea
events.text: Marcellus attacks the sea wall of Achradina with sixty quinqueremes and ladders mounted on ships lashed in pairs.

events.title: Archimedes' claws
events.text: Iron claws on cranes lift the Roman ships by the bow and drop them; catapults hurl stones over the walls.

events.title: Assault by land
events.text: Appius Claudius attacks the Hexapylon gate and is driven back by Archimedes' artillery.

events.title: Himilco lands
events.text: Himilco lands at Heraclea Minoa with twenty thousand infantry, three thousand cavalry and twelve elephants.

events.title: Agrigentum taken
events.text: Himilco seizes Agrigentum, which becomes Carthage's base in Sicily.

events.title: Bomilcar's fleet
events.text: Fifty-five Carthaginian warships under Bomilcar slip into the Great Harbour of Syracuse.

events.title: Megara sacked
events.text: Marcellus storms and sacks Megara Hyblaea, north of Syracuse.

events.title: Massacre at Henna
events.text: Fearing betrayal, the Roman garrison commander Pinarius has the citizens of Henna cut down in their assembly.

events.title: Morgantina defects
events.text: Morgantina goes over to the Carthaginians with the Roman grain stored there.

events.title: Arpi retaken
events.text: The consul Fabius recaptures the Apulian city of Arpi from Hannibal.

events.title: Festival of Artemis
events.text: While the city feasts in honour of Artemis, Roman soldiers scale the wall near the Galeagra tower by night.

events.title: Epipolae falls
events.text: The Hexapylon gate is opened at dawn and Marcellus takes the heights of Epipolae.

events.title: Euryalus surrenders
events.text: The great fortress of Euryalus at the western tip of Epipolae surrenders.

events.title: Plague in the marshes
events.text: Disease in the marshes by the Anapus wipes out the Carthaginian relief army with Himilco and Hippocrates.

events.title: Bomilcar turns back
events.text: Bomilcar's fleet of 130 warships and 700 transports turns away at Cape Pachynus and sails for Tarentum.

events.title: Moericus opens a gate
events.text: The Spanish officer Moericus lets the Romans into the Island, Ortygia; the rest of the city surrenders.

events.title: Death of Archimedes
events.text: Absorbed in figures drawn in the sand, Archimedes is killed by a Roman soldier, against Marcellus' orders.

events.title: Tarentum betrayed
events.text: Tarentine conspirators let Hannibal into Tarentum by night; the Roman garrison holds out in the citadel.

events.title: Capua besieged
events.text: Three Roman armies surround Capua with a double line of siege works.

events.title: Hannibal at Rome
events.text: To relieve Capua, Hannibal marches to within three miles of Rome, then turns back.

events.title: Capua falls
events.text: Capua surrenders; many of its senators take poison and dozens more are executed.

events.title: Battle of the Himera
events.text: Marcellus defeats Hanno and Epicydes after Hanno snubs Muttines and the Numidian cavalry leave the field.

events.title: Spoils of Syracuse
events.text: Marcellus enters Rome in ovation with the statues, paintings and machines of Syracuse.

events.title: Muttines' revenge
events.text: Removed from command by Hanno, Muttines has his Numidians seize Agrigentum's sea gate for the consul Laevinus.

events.title: Agrigentum enslaved
events.text: Laevinus beheads Agrigentum's leaders and sells the rest of its people into slavery.

events.title: Sicily subdued
events.text: Twenty towns are betrayed, six stormed and forty surrender; Laevinus sets the island to growing grain for Rome.

events.title: Salapia betrayed
events.text: Salapia is handed back to Rome, with its garrison of Numidian horsemen.

events.title: Defeat at Herdonia
events.text: Hannibal destroys the army of the proconsul Fulvius Centumalus at Herdonia.

chartNote: Share of the area of today's Italian provinces in view, by the side that held most of each. Ancient cities and peoples did not follow these modern lines, and many provinces held towns on both sides; the map is a simplification, and its sources are mostly Roman. Carthage, Malta and Macedon lie outside the coloured regions.
